MCMC posterior sampling, equilibration, and simulated annealing for SBMs

mcmc_sweep.Rd

Native C++ Metropolis-Hastings and merge-split Markov chain Monte Carlo samplers for flat and nested microcanonical stochastic block models, targeting the exact posterior \(P(\mathbf{b} \mid A) \propto \exp(-\beta \Sigma(\mathbf{b}))\). These are the R counterparts of graph-tool's mcmc_sweep(), multiflip_mcmc_sweep(), mcmc_equilibrate(), and mcmc_anneal().

Usage

mcmc_sweep(state, beta = 1, niter = 1L, c = NULL, d = 0.01,
  multiflip = TRUE, B_min = 1L, B_max = Inf, psingle = NULL,
  psplit = 1, pmerge = 1, pmergesplit = 1, gibbs_sweeps = 10L,
  ls_shuffle = TRUE)
mcmc_equilibrate(state, wait = 1000L, nbreaks = 2L, max_niter = Inf,
  force_niter = NULL, epsilon = 0, multiflip = TRUE, mcmc_args = list(),
  history = FALSE, callback = NULL, collect = FALSE, thin = 1L,
  verbose = FALSE)
mcmc_anneal(state, beta_range = c(1, 10), niter = 100L,
  history = FALSE, mcmc_equilibrate_args = list(), verbose = FALSE)
sample_posterior(state, nsamples = 1000L, thin = 10L, burnin = NULL,
  multiflip = TRUE, mcmc_args = list(), equilibrate_args = list(),
  history = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

state

A flat block state from block_state, minimize_blockmodel_dl, weighted_block_state, minimize_weighted_blockmodel_dl, layered_block_state, minimize_layered_blockmodel_dl, pp_block_state, minimize_pp_blockmodel_dl, ranked_block_state, or minimize_ranked_blockmodel_dl, or a nested block state from nested_block_state, minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl, nested_weighted_block_state, minimize_nested_weighted_blockmodel_dl, nested_layered_block_state, minimize_nested_layered_blockmodel_dl, nested_ranked_block_state, or minimize_nested_ranked_blockmodel_dl.

beta

Inverse temperature (\(\beta \ge 0\), or Inf for greedy zero-temperature moves). Posterior sampling uses beta = 1.

niter

Number of sweeps per call (for mcmc_sweep), or number of exponential cooling steps (for mcmc_anneal).

c

Ergodic proposal smoothing parameter (\(c \ge 0\); Inf gives uniform proposals). Defaults to 0.5 for flat states and 1 (scaled by \(2^l\) at level \(l\)) for nested states. Nested states also accept a numeric vector of per-level values.

d

Probability in \([0, 1)\) of proposing a new (empty) group during a single-node move.

multiflip

If TRUE (the default), use merge-split MCMC combining single-node moves, group splits, group merges, and merge-split moves; if FALSE, use single-node Metropolis-Hastings sweeps only.

B_min, B_max

Bounds on the number of occupied groups (applied to level 0 for nested states).

psingle, psplit, pmerge, pmergesplit

Relative move-type weights for merge-split MCMC. psingle = NULL defaults to the number of nodes at the current level.

gibbs_sweeps

Number of Gibbs sweeps used to refine split and merge-split proposals (at least 1).

ls_shuffle

For nested states, whether to randomize the order in which hierarchy levels are swept.

wait, nbreaks, max_niter, force_niter, epsilon

Equilibration controls matching graph-tool's mcmc_equilibrate(): waits for nbreaks consecutive intervals of wait iterations without a record-breaking change in description length, up to max_niter iterations (or runs exactly force_niter iterations when specified).

mcmc_args

Named list of arguments forwarded to mcmc_sweep().

history

Whether to return a data frame recording nattempts, nmoves, entropy, and beta at each iteration.

callback

Optional R function called as callback(state) after each iteration. When NULL, the entire equilibration loop runs in C++.

collect

Whether to collect sampled partitions (every thin iterations) during equilibration.

thin

Thinning interval (number of equilibration steps between collected samples).

verbose

Whether to print iteration progress.

beta_range

Numeric vector of length 2 giving the starting and ending inverse temperatures for exponential cooling.

mcmc_equilibrate_args

Named list of equilibration arguments used at each annealing step.

nsamples

Number of thinned posterior partitions to collect.

burnin

Number of burn-in sweeps before sampling. When NULL (the default), runs mcmc_equilibrate() with equilibrate_args first.

equilibrate_args

Named list of equilibration controls used when burnin = NULL.

Details

Single-node moves use Peixoto's neighbor-based ergodic proposal with exact forward and reverse Hastings probabilities. Merge-split sweeps combine single-node moves with group splits, group merges, and merge-split moves refined by gibbs_sweeps conditional Gibbs sweeps using an auxiliary-variable Hastings ratio that preserves exact detailed balance for any gibbs_sweeps >= 1 and any finite \(\beta \ge 0\).

For nested states at level \(l < L - 1\), new groups created by single-node moves or splits inherit the parent label at level \(l + 1\); correspondingly, emptying a singleton group or merging two groups at level \(l\) is restricted to groups sharing the same parent, while moves at level \(l + 1\) reassign groups across parents. This maintains ergodicity and exact detailed balance over unlabelled hierarchies.

Unlike Python's mutating methods, these R functions treat states as immutable and return the updated state in the $state element of the result. All random draws use R's RNG, so set.seed() reproduces trajectories. As with any MCMC sampler on multimodal posteriors, record-breaking equilibration is a heuristic and does not guarantee global mixing across well-separated modes.

Value

mcmc_sweep(), mcmc_equilibrate(), and mcmc_anneal() return a list with the updated state, final entropy, cumulative dS, nattempts, nmoves, niter, and optionally history and samples. sample_posterior() returns a list with final state, samples (list of 1-based partitions or nested hierarchies), nested, equilibration, and sampling.

References

Peixoto, T. P. (2014). Efficient Monte Carlo and greedy heuristic for the inference of stochastic block models. Physical Review E 89, 012804. doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.89.012804

Peixoto, T. P. (2020). Merge-split Markov chain Monte Carlo for community detection. Physical Review E 102, 012305. doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.102.012305

See also

partition_mode_state, mode_cluster_state, plot_marginals, demo("posterior_sampling")

Examples

g <- graph_create(12, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(t(combn(1:6, 2)), t(combn(7:12, 2)), c(1, 7)))
set.seed(1)
fit <- minimize_blockmodel_dl(g)
post <- sample_posterior(fit, nsamples = 50, thin = 2, burnin = 20)
pm <- partition_mode_state(post)
pm
#> <partition mode: M = 50, B = 3, uncertainty = 0.1200, DL = 257.5850 nats>
